messages.author: 3841b7341e53f8aa
messages.subject: Combining trajectory and for loop functions
parts:
Hi,
I have the following problem: I would like to combine a (double) for loop function with the trajectory function but it did not woked how I tried. The problem is the following:
- there are 5 customer orders (dummy0,...dummy4)
- production ordrers (let´s say for different types of components of the endproduct) are generated from the customer orders (with the help of clones)
- 1 customer order can have 1 or max. 2 production orders (so 1 or 2 type of components) (bs_1 and bs_2)
- there are 3 stations: station1(commissioning), station2(assembly of components), final assembly (clones will be joined here) - so station 1 and station 2 can have clones
- as you can see from dataframe B:
- production order dummy1 has 1 clones (2 pieces from bs_1 and 4 pieces from bs_2 must be produced),
- but production order dummy0 needs just one tpye of component(bs_2) so theoretically just one original trajetory is needed and no clone at all

What I would like to do: generating the trajectories just where a production order is needed, so where dataframe B has a number different from 0:

for (i in 1:nrow(B)) {
   for (j in 1:ncol(B)){
      if (B[i,j]!=0) {
      #generate trajectory
      }
   }
}

I copied the trajectory definition function into the highlighted place (#generate trajectory) but Simmer says: `trajectory`is not a valid trajectory

If you have any idea, how it could be solved, I would appriciate your efforts.
Thanks a lot in advance.
Regards,
Viola


Here you can find the code:

library(simmer)

env <- simmer()

bs_1 <- c(0,2,3,4,2)
bs_2 <- c(5,4,0,0,3)
B <- data.frame(bs_1, bs_2)
rownames(B) <- c("dummy0","dummy1","dummy2","dummy3","dummy4")

t <- trajectory() %>%
       clone(n=2,
              trajectory("traj1_bs1") %>%
               # Station1 - com
               log_("enter st1_cl1") %>%
               set_attribute("enter time st1_cl1", function(){now(env)}) %>%
               log_(function() {paste("Number of modules_cl1:",B[get_name(env),"bs_1"])})%>%
               set_prioritization(function() {c(sample(1:5,1), NA, NA)},mod="+") %>%
               seize("resource1") %>%
               log_(function() {paste("waited before st1_cl1: ", now(env)-get_attribute(env, "enter time st1_cl1"))}) %>%
               timeout(function() {B[get_name(env),"bs_1"]*rnorm(1,1,0.5)}) %>%
               release("resource1")  %>%
               log_(function(){paste("end st1_cl1:", now(env))}) %>%
               # Station2 - ass
               set_attribute("start time st2_cl1", function(){now(env)}) %>%
               set_prioritization(function() {c(sample(1:5,1), NA, NA)},mod="+") %>%
               seize("resource2") %>%
               log_(function() {paste("waited before st2-cl1: ", now(env)-get_attribute(env, "start time st2_cl1"))}) %>%
               timeout(function() {B[get_name(env),"bs_1"]*rnorm(1,2,1)}) %>%
               release("resource2")  %>%
               log_(function(){paste("finish st2_cl1:", now(env))}),
             trajectory("traj2_bs2") %>%
               # Station1 - com
               log_("enter st1_cl2") %>%
               set_attribute("enter time st1_cl2", function(){now(env)}) %>%
               log_(function() {paste("Number of modules_cl2",B[get_name(env),"bs_2"])})%>%
               set_prioritization(function() {c(sample(1:5,1), NA, NA)},mod="+") %>%
               seize("resource1") %>%
               log_(function() {paste("waited before st1_cl2: ", now(env)-get_attribute(env, "enter time st1_cl2"))}) %>%
               timeout(function() {B[get_name(env),"bs_2"]*rnorm(1,1,0.5)}) %>%
               release("resource1")  %>%
               log_(function(){paste("end st1_cl2:", now(env))}) %>%
               # Station2 - ass
               set_attribute("start time st2_cl2", function(){now(env)}) %>%
               set_prioritization(function() {c(sample(1:5,1), NA, NA)},mod="+") %>%
               seize("resource2") %>%
               log_(function() {paste("waited before st2_cl2: ", now(env)-get_attribute(env, "start time st2_cl2"))}) %>%
               timeout(function() {B[get_name(env),"bs_2"]*rnorm(1,2,1)}) %>%
               release("resource2")  %>%
               log_(function(){paste("finish st2_cl2:", now(env))})) %>%
          # final assembly
          synchronize(wait = TRUE, mon_all = TRUE) %>%
          log_("start endm") %>%
          set_attribute("start endm", function(){now(env)}) %>%
          seize("endm") %>%
          log_(function() {paste("waited before endm: ", now(env)-get_attribute(env, "start endm"))}) %>%
          timeout(function() {rnorm(1,2,1)}) %>%
          release("endm") %>%
          log_(function(){paste("ready endm, leave: ", now(env))})
#plot(t)

env %>%
  add_resource("resource1") %>%
  add_resource("resource2") %>%
  add_resource("endm") %>%
  add_generator("dummy", t, at(rep(0, 5))) %>%
  run() %>%
  get_mon_arrivals()

I'm not sure what you are trying to achieve here. A trajectory is not
a function.

If I understand the problem correctly, I would add another column
"time", with the arrival times, to the data frame, and then I would
use add_dataframe instead of add_generator (see ?add_dataframe). bs_1
and bs_2 will be automatically defined as attributes for each arrival,
and you can use them in your trajectory below.

I see also that you are printing the waiting time for each resource.
You don't need to do that, because simmer is automatically monitoring
this information for you. You can retrieve this at the end of the
simulation using get_mon_arrivals(per_resource=TRUE).
